### Addendum — the remedy this card recommends has its own failure mode, and the fix should say so

Epic PM `session_015c5G6TmpMKgnusmTpD7Ntt`, 2026-09-13T15:44Z. From the at-tier review of PR #18016 (record `5654272242`), which read the script independently and **agrees with this card's diagnosis** — adding one detail and one caveat.

**Confirming detail.** The script partitions conflicts *solely* by membership in `.gitattributes`' `merge=os-regen` list — the review measured **0 references to `regen-artifacts.mjs`** anywhere in it, so generatedness is never consulted. And the self-test does not cover this class: **case 6 exercises only driver-routed `mixed:` rows, not `NOT_DRIVER_MANAGED` rows carrying a `gen:`**. ⇒ the gap is unpinned as well as unhandled, which matters because #14671's fix *was* pinned that way and still left this limb.

**⚠️ The caveat, which the fix should carry.** The correct resolution for this class — *take either side to reach a committable state, commit the merge, then regenerate and commit that* — is what PR #18016's round did, and it was sound **there**. But it is only sound under two conditions, and a green gate does not establish either:

`check:migration-registry` exit 0 proves **`registry.ts == f(entries/)`** and nothing more. It is sufficient only when

1. `entries/` is the **union** of both sides, and
2. **no prose was edited outside the generated regions** on the side that was discarded.

Both were measured true on #18016 — the review checked prose outside the conflict markers at 1913 = 1913 and 1928 = 1928, and confirmed `entries/` is exactly `sort -u` of the two sides. But nothing in the tooling *checks* those conditions.

⇒ **A hand-edited rationale sitting outside the generated regions on the discarded side would be dropped silently, with every gate green.** That is the same silent-loss shape `.gitattributes:36` exists to prevent, reached by the remedy rather than by the mistake.

So whichever way class 3's message is worded, it should not stop at "resolve by regeneration". It should also tell the operator to **check the discarded side for edits outside the generated regions before taking it** — or, better, have the script make that check itself, since it already has both blobs in hand at the moment it prints.

⛔ Not proposing the implementation; that is the owning seat's call. Recorded because a fix that only corrects the *label* would leave an operator following correct instructions into a silent drop.

**Evidence transplant from the `domain:spec` seat** (`session_01EfsizFDgAcEjpwv4oM3WGT`) — I filed **#18062** on the same root cause ~28 minutes after this card and am closing mine as its duplicate. This card is earlier, filed at the maintainer's direction, and digs further into the script mechanism (including distinguishing itself from #14671). Below is the part of mine that is **not** in this card: the live behavioural consequence and the detection gap.

## It is not only a routing misclassification — it silently changed behaviour

On PR #17835's second `origin/main` merge, `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts` conflicted and was resolved the way this card's misrouting invites: **take a side + regenerate**.

That file is generated **only between its `os-generated` markers**. `step18.conversionIds` and `step18.rationale` are hand-authored append regions **outside** them — the file's own header says so: *"`conversionIds`, and the two tables' load-bearing doc comments — is still hand-written and still merges as text."*

The resolution restored every generated row and **silently dropped both hand-authored edits**. Consequence, quoting the round that hit it:

> without `'page-assigned-profiles-removed'` in `step18.conversionIds` the 17→18 hop stops applying the conversion, so a replayed page **keeps** `assignedProfiles`.

⇒ behavioural, not cosmetic.

## ⭐ The detection gap — this is the part worth carrying

> The **115-family gate sweep was GREEN** on that same tree.

What caught it was `migrations.test.ts`'s chain-replay composability test (`Test Files 1 failed | 475 passed`, with `assignedProfiles` still present) — and **only because a fixture happened to exercise the dropped id**. A conversion whose fixture does not exercise it would have merged silently.

Fixed in `4d55c069c`, which restores both hand-authored regions keeping main's entries alongside the branch's; re-running the generator afterwards is byte-identical, which is itself the proof the restored lines sit outside the generated regions.

## Why this raises the stakes on the fix

This card's mechanism means the misrouting is not a one-off: **any** PR that merges `main` while touching a protocol step hits it, the documented remedy destroys one side, and detection depends on a fixture coincidence rather than any gate. ⛔ I am not prescribing the fix — scope and ownership are not this seat's to set.
